intro: This course covered how infection spreads, standard precautions, hand hygiene, PPE, safe handling of sharps, waste and spillages, and recognising sepsis.
points: Sepsis is a life-threatening emergency — if you see confusion, mottled skin or fast breathing, call 999 and say you suspect sepsis.
Clean hands at the WHO 5 Moments — your most powerful tool — using soap and water for C. difficile and norovirus.
Apply standard precautions to everyone, every time — you can rarely tell just by looking who is carrying a harmful organism.
Put PPE on as apron, mask, eyes then gloves, and take it off gloves, apron, eyes then mask, cleaning hands afterwards.
Never re-sheath a used needle — drop it straight into a rigid sharps bin, and report any needlestick injury immediately.
Report an outbreak early — two or more linked cases — and follow control measures like isolation and enhanced cleaning.
